quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What factors affect how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
Presence of a stop sign.
Use of your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if another car is about to hit you?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: What should you do when a driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Speed up.
Go the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This creates space in front of your vehicle so the other driver can complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: When should you use turn signals when parking at a curb?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling up to the curb.
When pulling up to or pulling away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling up to or pulling away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals when pulling up to a curb or when pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?

options.text: Speed limit.
Stop.
Hospital.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign is always a stop sign. Come to a complete stop when you see this red sign.

questions.question: Can you park in the access aisles next to handicap parking spaces?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: No one can park in handicap parking access aisles. These spaces are needed for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing.
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and watch for traffic before proceeding.

questions.question: What should you check before starting the engine?

options.text: Only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
All passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: All passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before you start the engine, make sure you and all passengers have buckled your seat belts. Make this part of your routine every time you drive.

questions.question: What must you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Signal for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road and stop. Let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over and stop.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic, if you can.
Speed up to keep your right-of-way.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic, if you can.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, you should make room to let vehicles merge into your lane.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. Solid white lines mean do not cross. Broken white lines mean you can cross to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, what should you do?

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match the traffic flow, and merge when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match the traffic flow, and merge when the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Do not stop. Use the acceleration lane to speed up and blend smoothly with the fast-moving traffic already on the highway.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and hold the pedal.
Grip the wheel tightly and use light braking.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the wheel tightly and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and using light brakes. Avoid stopping on the road. Move to a safe spot off the road.

questions.question: This sign warns you that you are approaching:

options.text: An intersection.
A crosswalk.
A railroad crossing.
A blasting zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic in the lanes you plan to enter. Be ready to stop if needed. You can continue without stopping if there is no traffic in your way.

questions.question: On a freeway, look farther ahead than you would on a city street:

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
Because it helps you keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Watch for traffic changes on the freeway. Look for signals from other drivers. Watch for vehicles merging and be ready for fast changes in road conditions and traffic.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes means:

options.text: Both lanes are going the same direction.
Passing is allowed when it is safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines separate lanes going opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They use vibration and sound to alert drivers that they have left the travel lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use vibration and sound to alert drivers that they have left the travel lane.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or red light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn at this intersection.

questions.question: A police officer tells you to drive through a red light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions. An officer's instructions override traffic signals and signs.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to an officer?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic violation.
Only if you are stopped and cited.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a traffic violation.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance while driving. Show it to an officer whenever you are stopped for a traffic violation or are in a collision.

questions.question: What should you do if your tire blows out?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes hard and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If you have a blowout, take your foot off the accelerator and slow down gradually. Do not brake hard until the vehicle has slowed down significantly.

questions.question: Which of these drugs can affect your driving?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold remedies
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: On a four-lane highway, do you have to stop when meeting a stopped school bus from the opposite direction?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You do not need to stop for a school bus on the opposite side of a four-lane highway. However, always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is turning left, what can they do?

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. Be prepared to see a bicyclist in the left lane when they are turning.

questions.question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to have total control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles can be unpredictable. Young riders often make sudden changes in direction. Remember that children and bicycles are small and hard to see.
